content.text: {"headline":"Recommend no action (P0): service level is predicted at 100% for 16:15-18:15 on both queues, at no extra cost.","why":"The earlier spike was caused by the P1 card authorisation gateway outage opened at 12:37. Payments calls reached 240 against 108 forecast in the 12:30 interval, and card_declined calls ran at 2.48x normal. Service level fell to 2.9% with 84 abandoned calls. Staffing was only 3-4 agents below plan, so the cause was extra calls, not missing staff. For the disruption window of 16:15-18:15, both payments and general are predicted at 100% service level with 0% abandons, well above the 80% target. Rest of day is predicted at 96%. No intervention is needed to meet target, so the cheapest compliant plan is to leave staffing as is.","trade_offs":["P1, moving 1 cross-skilled agent from payments to general at 19:00-20:00, also costs INR 0 and predicts the same results: 100% in the window and 96% rest of day. It adds no measurable benefit and takes a payments agent away from the outage-affected queue.","Neither plan has any policy violations or extra cost, so the choice comes down to keeping things simple and avoiding unnecessary risk to payments."],"watch":"Keep an eye on the card gateway incident status and on card_declined call volume. If the outage resumes or payments demand climbs again, service level could drop quickly, so re-run the plan. No escalation to the duty manager is flagged."}
